translationRepairs: [Qi Records 2] From Shangzhang Zhixu through Xuanyi Dunzang—six years in all.
[Qi Records 2] From Efeng Kundun through Tuwei Dahuangluo—six years in all.
The Chinese 閼逢困敦 and 屠維大荒落 are the Erya year-names for jiazi and jisi; "Shangzhang Zhixu" and "Xuanyi Dunzang" are different year-names not in the source.
Liu Yun, Wang Sengru, Jiang Ge of Jiyang, Fan Zhen, and Kong Xiuyuan of Kuaiji were among them as well.

Legal Affairs Officer Liu Yun, Imperial Academy Erudite Wang Sengru, South Xu Province presented scholar Jiang Ge of Jiyang, Palace Gentleman of the Masters of Writing Fan Zhen, and Kong Xiuyuan of Kuaiji were among them as well.
The idiomatic version omits the offices and credentials 法曹參軍, 太學博士, 南徐州秀才 and 尚書殿中郎 that the Chinese gives for these men.
Chen was the son of a younger brother of Hui Kai;
Chen was a nephew (a brother's son) of Hui Kai;
從子 means a brother's son; the Chinese does not say the brother was younger, so "younger" is an invention.
Commentators held that the emperor surpassed Cao Pi of Wei but fell short of Emperor Ming of Han.
Commentators held that the emperor surpassed Emperor Wen of Wei but fell short of Emperor Ming of Han.
The Chinese 魏文 is the posthumous title Emperor Wen of Wei; rendering it with the personal name Cao Pi is inconsistent with the parallel 漢明 (Emperor Ming of Han).

Huang loved martial display; when he left South Xuzhou he secretly brought back several hundred men's weapons to Jiankang, was discovered by the prohibition office, and they were thrown into the Yangtze.

Huang loved martial display; when he left South Xuzhou he secretly brought back weapons for several hundred men to Jiankang; this was discovered by the prohibition office, and they were thrown into the Yangtze.
The literal version makes Huang the subject of "was discovered" and then switches to "they", a grammatical failure; 為禁司所覺 refers to the smuggling being discovered.

In the sixth month, on gengxu, Northern Wei promoted the Prince of Henan, Chief Tuyuhun, to General of Chariots and Cavalry and sent Palace Attendant Qiu Guanxian of Wuxing as envoy to Henan, also escorting a Rouran envoy.

In the sixth month, on gengxu, Northern Wei promoted the Prince of Henan, Duyihou, to General of Chariots and Cavalry and sent Palace Attendant Qiu Guanxian of Wuxing as envoy to Henan, also escorting a Rouran envoy.
度易侯 is the personal name (Duyihou) of the Prince of Henan; "Chief Tuyuhun" is not in the Chinese and replaces the name with a people-name.

員外散騎常侍 is rendered elsewhere in this chapter as "Supernumerary Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry"; 散騎 is not "Rapid Cavalry" and 常侍 is not "Palace Attendant".

族弟 specifies a younger clansman of the same generation; the English drops "younger", which the kinship term states.

On wuzi Prince Niao of Yuzhang was appointed Grand Marshal, Xiao Ziliang of Prince of Zhangling was made Minister over the Masses, and Prince Ying of Linchuan, General of the Guards Wang Jian, and General of the Central Army Wang Jingze were all granted the added title of Grand General with staff equal to the Three Excellencies.

On wuzi Prince Yi of Yuzhang was appointed Grand Marshal, Ziliang, Prince of Zhangling was made Minister over the Masses, and Prince Ying of Linchuan, General of the Guards Wang Jian, and General of the Central Army Wang Jingze were all granted the added title of Grand General with staff equal to the Three Excellencies.
嶷 is read Yi here (the prince's given name), not "Niao"; 章陵王子良 gives title + given name, the surname Xiao is not in the text and "X of Prince of Y" is ungrammatical.

桓玄宗族 names Huan Xuan personally; "Eastern Jin" is not in the text and the person name is lost.
